items.headline: Bitdeer AI adds 60MW (A103) in Cyberjaya under an 8-year services agreement; campus to reach ~71.5MW
items.detail: A103 is designed for liquid-cooled NVIDIA rack-scale systems, with energisation expected in 1Q2028. The Cyberjaya campus would total about 71.5MW of AI cloud capacity (critical IT load), per the company.

sources.publisher: Bitdeer AI press release (GlobeNewswire via Nasdaq)

items.note: Released 12 Oct 2026 4:30pm EDT (13 Oct MYT). Company-stated figures; timeline is a forecast.
items.soWhat: Malaysia is winning the next generation of liquid-cooled AI capacity, not just conventional colocation.
items.opportunity: Demand for liquid-cooling, power and fit-out contractors on the Cyberjaya campus.
items.watchOut: Energisation targeted for 1Q2028, a company forecast.

items.headline: Deep Source locks in 10-year colocation for 67MW AI data centre in Prai, Penang; 26MW due by Mar 2027
items.detail: Deep Source (PN) signed a master colocation agreement on 2 Oct covering 67MW, plus a 7 Oct letter of intent with Longmotive DC Solutions for building and M&E works: 26MW targeted by 31 Mar 2027 and 41MW by 30 Jun 2027.
items.note: Customer not named. Completion dates are targets, subject to certification.
items.soWhat: Penang is emerging as an AI data-centre node beyond Johor and Klang Valley.
items.opportunity: Building and M&E works (LOI with Longmotive) point to near-term fit-out demand.
items.watchOut: Customer unnamed; completion subject to certification.

items.headline: Realord signs MOU for a possible Johor AI data centre of up to 300MW (first phase ~100MW)
items.detail: Phased project, first phase about 100MW; involves land acquisition in Johor and is subject to definitive agreements and regulatory approvals.
items.note: Status: MOU only; the company warns it may not materialise.
items.soWhat: Signals continued foreign interest in Johor capacity, but nothing is committed.
items.watchOut: Proposal only: non-binding MOU, subject to land, definitive agreements and approvals.

items.headline: MITI approves Privasia unit's Bagan Datuk data centre, conditional on off-grid power of up to 50MW
items.detail: Approval (letter dated 7 Sept 2026) is conditional on securing an off-grid energy supply with maximum demand of 50MW, in line with Energy Commission and RE frameworks.
items.soWhat: Approvals now hinge on power sourcing; off-grid supply is becoming a precondition.
items.watchOut: Subject to securing off-grid energy within Energy Commission and RE frameworks.

items.headline: S P Setia (2Q26 sales RM864mil) backs Budget 2027 first-home relief up to RM750,000 and Johor focus
items.detail: Cites the first-home stamp-duty relief up to RM750,000 to 2030, JS-SEZ focus and Green Investment Tax Allowance for its Setia Fontaines Industrial Park. 2Q26 sales were RM864mil; net profit RM98.06mil (2Q25: RM99.8mil).
items.soWhat: A large developer reads the Budget as supportive for townships and Johor industrial land.
items.opportunity: JS-SEZ and Green Investment Tax Allowance support industrial park plays such as Setia Fontaines.
items.watchOut: 2Q26 net profit dipped to RM98.06mil from RM99.8mil.

items.headline: Budget 2027: first-home stamp duty waived up to RM500,000, and on the first RM500,000 of homes up to RM750,000, for 2027-2030 SPAs
items.detail: Full exemption up to RM500,000; for RM500,001-RM750,000, the first RM500,000 is fully exempt and the balance 50%. Abandoned-project revivals get full exemption; SJKP guarantees of up to RM20bil target about 80,000 first-time buyers.
items.note: Proposals; effective subject to the Finance Bill.
items.soWhat: Lowers buyers' upfront cash need in the core mass-market band; RM20bil SJKP guarantees widen the pool to ~80,000 self-employed first-time buyers.
items.opportunity: Products priced at or below RM750,000 for first-time buyers.
items.watchOut: Proposal only, subject to the Finance Bill; applies to Malaysian citizens' first homes.

items.headline: Rehda asks government to extend first-home stamp-duty relief to homes up to RM1mil
items.detail: Developers' association welcomed the Budget housing measures but said material, labour and regulatory costs keep pressuring affordability.
items.soWhat: Industry signals costs, not demand, are the affordability bottleneck.
items.watchOut: Rising material, labour and regulatory charges continue to pressure margins.

items.headline: IJM wins RM1.23bil AT&S semiconductor plant in Kulim; order book rises to ~RM10.6bil
items.detail: Design-and-build of production, central utility and wastewater buildings; starts 4Q2026 with a 14-month programme. Order book about RM10.6bil after the award, following RM909.5mil of semiconductor and medtech wins in August.
items.note: IJM cites its IBS capabilities for delivery.
items.soWhat: Semiconductor fast-track builds are becoming a large, repeatable contract pool for top-tier contractors.
items.opportunity: Follows RM909.5mil of August semiconductor/medtech wins; IBS used for delivery certainty.

items.headline: GDB proposes RM81.6mil buy of 51% of two Sarawak contractors, lifting order book to RM741.81mil
items.detail: Consideration RM40.8mil cash plus 96.91 million shares at 42 sen; vendors guarantee cumulative PAT of at least RM45mil (Jul 2026-Dec 2028). Order book would rise to RM741.81mil. GDB also plans entry into property development with a RM500mil GDV Kuching project.
items.note: Status: proposed; gross proceeds RM70.83mil-RM183.48mil depending on take-up. Dilution is a watch-out.
items.soWhat: Scales GDB into Sarawak and property development (RM500mil GDV Kuching project).
items.opportunity: Vendors guarantee cumulative PAT of at least RM45mil for Jul 2026-Dec 2028.
items.watchOut: Proposal only; funded by placement of up to 30% plus rights issue, so dilution.

items.headline: Budget 2027 reintroduces the variation-of-price mechanism for construction inputs such as diesel and bitumen
items.detail: Says the mechanism will help contractors manage swings in inputs such as diesel and bitumen.
items.soWhat: Reduces contractors' exposure to input-cost swings on public jobs.
items.watchOut: Scope and eligible contracts not detailed in the source.

items.headline: Palm oil stocks jump 24.54% to 3.51mil tonnes in September; exports fall 12.13% to 1.12mil t
items.detail: CPO production rose 16.48% m-o-m to 2.117mil t; palm oil exports fell 12.13% to 1.120mil t; CPO stocks up 31.88% to 2.163mil t.
items.soWhat: Inventory overhang caps near-term CPO prices.

items.headline: Kenanga holds 2027 CPO assumption at RM4,700/t despite 10-year-high stocks; sector kept at Neutral
items.detail: Analyst view: inventory 3.511mil t (+49% y-o-y); CPO assumptions RM4,500/t (2026) and RM4,700/t (2027), citing biodiesel demand and El Nino supply risk in 2027; warns of cost inflation.
items.soWhat: Analyst view: biodiesel demand and El Nino could tighten 2027 supply.
items.watchOut: Forecast only; cost inflation risk to margins.

items.headline: Malaysia-EU FTA 80% done, signing targeted by end-June 2027; palm oil and autos unresolved
items.detail: MITI minister Johari Abdul Ghani targets signing by end-June 2027 and says major producers are preparing for the EUDR.
items.note: Target date is a government aim, not a commitment.
items.soWhat: EU market access for palm oil remains contingent on EUDR compliance.
items.opportunity: Major producers say they already meet EUDR requirements.
items.watchOut: Target date is a government aim, not a commitment.

items.headline: Budget 2027 gives RM1,500 one-off aid to 1.3mil civil servants and RM750 to pensioners, in two instalments
items.detail: Covers Grade Utama B and below, including contract staff; instalments before Aidilfitri and ahead of the 70th Merdeka anniversary.
items.note: Interpretation: a one-off cash boost to civil-servant borrowers' disposable income, not a financing measure.
items.soWhat: Interpretation: modestly improves repayment capacity of civil-servant borrowers.
items.watchOut: One-off cash aid, not a financing measure; paid before Aidilfitri and before the 70th Merdeka anniversary.

items.headline: Budget 2027 commits RM15bil via TNB to the grid; industry warns grid and storage gaps could slow RE
items.detail: Also cites UEM Lestra RM1bil for projects incl. KLIA energy storage and a 1GW Johor hybrid project; green tech tax incentives extended to 31 Dec 2030.
items.note: Interpretation: grid capex is a demand driver for cable makers, but the article does not name any cable company.
items.soWhat: Interpretation: grid capex is a direct demand driver for power-cable makers.
items.opportunity: Grid, BESS and the 1GW Johor hybrid project imply cable call-ups.
items.watchOut: Article names no cable company; pace depends on connection approvals.

items.headline: HLIB lifts Southern Cable target to RM3.58; RM200mil DC and 132kV orders fill FY26 MV/HV capacity
items.detail: Analyst view: RM200mil of 2Q26 DC and 132kV orders have fully booked MV/HV capacity for FY26; 3Q26 revenue could reach RM600mil and FY26 sales top RM2bil.
items.note: Analyst estimates. Watch-out: higher plastic costs squeeze margins on TNB orders.
items.soWhat: Analyst view: data-centre orders are shifting the mix away from TNB.
items.watchOut: Higher plastic costs squeeze TNB-order margins.

items.headline: International arrivals reach 28.8mil in Jan-Aug 2026, up only 1.8% y-o-y
items.detail: Tourism Malaysia frames this under the Visit Malaysia 2026-2027 campaign; says tourism contributes over 15% of GDP.
items.note: Article summary box says 2023; the body is dated 2 Oct 2026 and refers to this year.
items.soWhat: Volume is rising slowly despite the Visit Malaysia 2026-2027 campaign.
items.watchOut: Low growth rate; no hotel occupancy data in the source.

keyTakeaways.headline: Data-centre and semiconductor capex is now feeding real construction orders
keyTakeaways.soWhat: IJM's RM1.23bil AT&S job and new Penang and Cyberjaya AI capacity show the tech build-out turning into contracts. The Johor 300MW plan is still only an MOU.

keyTakeaways.headline: Power is the binding constraint, and that is good for grid and cable suppliers
keyTakeaways.soWhat: MITI's Privasia approval requires off-grid power, and industry says grid and storage gaps could slow the RE rollout despite the RM15bil TNB grid commitment. Cable makers like Southern Cable are booked out on DC and HV orders (analyst view).

keyTakeaways.headline: Budget 2027 helps first-home buyers, but developers say costs are the real issue
keyTakeaways.soWhat: The stamp-duty relief up to RM750,000 and SJKP guarantees support entry-level demand from 2027. Rehda and S P Setia both point to building costs; the returning variation-of-price mechanism helps contractors absorb input swings.

keyTakeaways.headline: Palm oil: record stocks against a firm 2027 price outlook
keyTakeaways.soWhat: September stocks of 3.51mil t point to near-term price pressure. Kenanga still assumes RM4,700/t for 2027 on biodiesel and El Nino (forecast), while EU FTA palm oil terms are unresolved.

keyTakeaways.headline: GDB moves into Sarawak and property, at the cost of dilution
keyTakeaways.soWhat: The proposed acquisitions would roughly double GDB's order book to RM741.81mil and add a RM500mil GDV Kuching project, funded by placement and rights. Shareholders face dilution, and the deal is still only a proposal.
